data.decision:
Reading order: D-export is the base; D-export-selection, D-export-templates and D-export-agent-enable refine it, and each says that everything else in D-export stands.

[D-export] Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-export): (1) `ddflow export <doc>` (CLI) and `ddflow_export` (MCP) generate documents from the event log: roadmap, bugs, rules, status, worklog, sessions, decisions index, changelog (and release notes for a version); printing to stdout is the default (review on demand, with --since/--version/--phase/--status/--limit, a size cap with an explicit truncation footer, --diff); writing needs --out/--update (CLI, interactive confirm on a TTY) or write=true plus a repo-relative path (MCP). All document tasks ship together (operator: all at once). (2) Default targets are at the REPO ROOT (ROADMAP.md, BUGS.md, RULES.md, STATUS.md, LOG.md, SESSION.md, CHANGELOG.md, DECISIONS.md), committed like any file; because they are not self-managed paths, every export target is registered as a [lease].shared_globs (generated) or append_only_globs (append mode) path automatically so no claim on them is needed; [export.<doc>].path overrides. (3) Update modes: whole generated file with a header carrying doc kind, ddflow version and a digest of the BODY (hand-edit detection; `--check` regenerates and compares exactly; no log digest); marker regions (<!-- ddflow:begin NAME --> ... <!-- ddflow:end NAME -->) inside hand-written files; append-only logs after the last exported event id. A hand-edited generated file or an unmarked file is never overwritten without --force. Writes are atomic under a lock. Paths outside the repo, symlinks, .git and .ddflow are refused. (4) Changelog: derive first (explicit field, then Conventional Commit prefix, then tags, then the 'fixes bug' title suffix, else Changed) with ONE optional field `changelog {category, line, skip}` set by `ddflow complete --changelog "Added: ..."`; `complete` never prompts and never requires it; the version of an item comes from git (merged_sha ancestor of the tag and not of the previous tag), nothing is reconstructed before the first tag. B167 is superseded; B174 narrows to version-file bumping; B202(b) becomes the export kind digest. (5) Safety: [export].redact is ON by default for every target (they are public-repo documents at the root), using services/redact_report.py, with 'redacted: N' in the header; free text from agents is fenced when served over MCP (reuse B-security-provenance's core/provenance.py, do not duplicate); replay is not an export kind. (6) Refresh: export may be refreshed automatically after merge or at phase close when the operator enables it ([export].refresh = off|merge|phase_close, default off; also expressible as a [cadence] entry); never without being enabled. (7) 'Rules' = decisions in force (by governing path) + lessons + the enforced workflow settings; imported rulebooks are not exported. (8) No new dependency (Jinja2 is already allowed); new optional event fields and the [export] section follow the forward-compat rule (B1c4a2346a9). run_nemo_run's frozen-file hooks stay the project's own decision (not touched here).

[D-export-selection] Operator 2026-10-02: it must be possible for the user to specify WHICH documents are generated, IF ANY, and to generate them on demand by asking the MCP, with the CLI, or as part of the phase document sync. (1) Nothing is generated or kept up to date unless selected: the default selection is EMPTY ([export].documents = []); `ddflow export` (no argument) lists every kind with its state (not selected / fresh / stale / hand-edited / missing) and `ddflow export enable <doc> [--path P] [--mode whole|region|append]` and `ddflow export disable <doc>` edit the selection (config write through the same guarded path as `config --set`, shared layer by default; --local for one machine); the MCP exposes the same list/enable/disable so an agent can ASK for a document without the operator editing TOML (enable is a config write: it follows the existing human-gate rules for settings that only the operator may change if any apply). (2) On demand, always possible regardless of the selection: `ddflow export <doc>` prints any kind to stdout (review) and with --out writes it; `ddflow export --all` acts on the selected set; the MCP `ddflow_export` does the same. (3) Phase document sync: the phase `docs` gate (D-docs-stage; B-docscheck/B-docs-gate-evidence) gains an export step: at phase close the selected documents are checked (`export --check`) and, when [export].refresh = docs_gate (or phase_close), regenerated first (`--update`), and the gate's evidence records the documents refreshed and their body digests (a hand-edited target is reported and skipped, never overwritten). [export].refresh values become off | merge | phase_close | docs_gate (default off). (4) The selection is per project, per document: each [export.<doc>] table may set its own refresh/redact/filters, so a project can keep CHANGELOG.md refreshed at the docs gate and ROADMAP.md only on request. Everything else in D-export stands.

[D-export-templates] Operator 2026-10-02 (refines D-export): the FORMAT of every exported document is owned by ddflow and defined by a Jinja2 template per document kind; the agent supplies no formatting (this also holds when ddflow runs as a remote or containerised MCP server: the server renders from the repository's data and templates, the client only receives or requests the result). (1) Every kind has a shipped default template ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2; resolution order: [export.<doc>].template (a path), then .ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2 in the project, then the shipped default - the same resolution as prompts (services/prompts.py). (2) `ddflow export eject <doc>` copies the shipped template into .ddflow/templates/export/ for editing (like `prompts eject`); `ddflow export <doc> --template PATH` renders once with an ad hoc template for review; `ddflow export validate [<doc>]` renders every selected document against the current data and reports template errors with file and line. (3) Query/grouping/filtering stays in Python (a pure (state, events, filters) -> data function per kind); the template receives ONLY that plain data (dicts, lists, strings, numbers) plus a small set of documented filters/helpers (e.g. md_escape, wrap, date, truncate, bar); it receives no objects with methods, no repo handle, no file or process access. (4) Templates are rendered in a Jinja2 SANDBOX (jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, StrictUndefined, no autoescape) because a template may come from a cloned repository: a template cannot reach Python internals, read files or run commands; a template that raises or times out is reported as a template error (exit 2 'could not run'), never as an empty clean document and never partially written. (5) The data contract per kind (the variable names, types and ordering) is documented in the README/help and carries a `schema_version` that the template can check; ddflow changes it compatibly (add fields, never rename or remove within a major) and notes changes in the release notes; the shipped templates are regression-tested against golden output. (6) A user override stays deterministic: same data + same template -> same bytes. The header (ddflow:generated marker + body digest) is added by ddflow around the template's body, not by the template, so a user template cannot remove hand-edit protection. (7) A ddflow upgrade never overwrites an ejected template: `ddflow export validate` and doctor note when the shipped default for a kind is newer than the ejected copy (compare a recorded shipped-template digest), like the driver-docs drift note.

[D-export-agent-enable] Operator 2026-10-02 (refines D-export-selection): an agent MAY enable a document (ddflow_export enable / `ddflow export enable`) without operator approval; the operator is only INFORMED and may later ask to stop it. So: (1) enabling by an agent is not refused and not gated; (2) it is always visible: the result says 'enabled <doc> -> <path> (by <agent>); the operator can stop it with ddflow export disable <doc>', an `export.enabled` record (agent, document, path, mode, time) is kept in the log, `ddflow export` lists who enabled each document and when, `brief` shows one line while any document was enabled by an agent and not yet acknowledged, and doctor notes it; (3) the operator stops it with `ddflow export disable <doc>` (CLI; also allowed to agents when the operator asks them to), and may VETO with `ddflow export disable <doc> --lock`: a locked document cannot be re-enabled by an agent (an agent's enable is refused with exit 3 'locked by the operator'), only unlocked by the operator at a terminal (refused under --agent/DDFLOW_AGENT/CLAUDECODE like `reviewers approve`); (4) an agent's enable only edits the shared selection and creates no file by itself: the first write happens on the next export run (on demand, merge, phase close or docs gate according to [export].refresh), never silently overwriting an existing hand-written or hand-edited file (the D-export rules). Everything else in D-export and D-export-selection stands.

data.alternatives:
[D9b8061fd38] Strict on file load (as dedupe.on_match and upgrade.skew were): rejected, an enum value added by a later release would make an older checkout unusable. Use-site checks only (core/flow.problems, api/ci unavailable): rejected, they never ran on write and most knobs had none.

[D6fc09b2590] Treat the fallback as not-a-config-layer so the recorded choice wins: rejected, a typo'd file meant to override the record, and the record may be looser than what was meant.
data.consequences:
[D9b8061fd38] dedupe.on_match and upgrade.skew become tolerant in files too. Use-site checks like api/ci's unknown on_merge mode are now reached only for a value set programmatically.

[D-enum-fallback-strict] A typo can only make ddflow more careful. A typo in a non-safety knob yields its declared strictest value, which may differ from the default; doctor says which value is in effect.

[D6fc09b2590] A typo in e.g. [flow].integration gives 'pr' even where 'flow choose integration merge' was recorded, until the typo is fixed; doctor and flow show both name it.

[D-fallback-no-remote] A typo in these two knobs keeps work local (direct merge, local claims) until fixed; doctor shows it.
data.context:
Consolidates D9b8061fd38, D-enum-fallback-strict, D6fc09b2590, D-fallback-no-remote into one current record (pure merge, operator authorisation 2026-10-15 under D-roadmap-review item 8). The old records are superseded by this one and keep their text in the log. Every section below is the recorded text of the source named in brackets, unchanged. D-enum-fallback-strict and D-fallback-no-remote were decided by the operator; D9b8061fd38 and D6fc09b2590 carry no operator attribution, so this record is attributed to the agent that merged them.

[D9b8061fd38] Bug Beea0744a7b: 21+ knobs listed choices only in comments, so typos were accepted silently. Refusing at file load would stop every command of an older checkout reading a config whose enum gained a value in a newer release (bugs Bcfc0d22a09, B9cb7dd1c3b, lesson L1907ee4695).

[D-enum-fallback-strict] bugfixI's fix for Beea0744a7b (D9b8061fd38) made a bad file value fall back to the default, so a typo in a deliberately tightened setting silently loosened it.

[D6fc09b2590] roborev (kilo) on B-enum-strict-fallback: a typo in a [flow] knob that is a workflow choice now sets sources to '<layer> (strictest fallback)', so choices.config_wins skips a recorded 'flow choose' value. Before, the knob stayed 'default' and the recorded choice applied.

[D-fallback-no-remote] B-enum-strict-fallback (8a9a35b9) chose pr/remote as strictest; both are fail-closed but reach the git remote.
data.decision:
Reading order (chronological, as the sources amend each other): D9b8061fd38 is the base; D-enum-fallback-strict changes its fallback from the default to the strictest value; D6fc09b2590 and D-fallback-no-remote refine that.

[D9b8061fd38] config.KNOB_CHOICES maps every enumerated knob to its allowed values and _KNOB_CHECKS derives a check from each. Config.check (config --set, ddflow_configure) and env vars refuse a value outside them. A config FILE carrying one is treated like an unknown knob: recorded in unknown_knobs, warned on stderr, reported by doctor, and the knob keeps its default -- all KNOB_CHOICES knobs are in _TOLERANT_VALUES.

[D-enum-fallback-strict] Operator 2026-10-05 (AskUserQuestion on D9b8061fd38): (1) keep file-load tolerance for every enum knob -- a bad value in a config file never stops loading; it is warned on stderr, recorded in unknown_knobs and reported by doctor; config --set, ddflow_configure and env vars still refuse; (2) CHANGED: the knob then takes its strictest allowed value (fail closed), not the shipped default -- e.g. enforce.stale_docs -> block, upgrade.skew -> refuse. Every KNOB_CHOICES entry declares its values in strictness order (or an explicit strictest value); a test requires every enum knob to declare it. For a knob with no safety dimension (e.g. flow.model, ci.on_merge, a display mode) the declared 'strictest' is the value that does the most checking or changes least (stated per knob in its doc); doctor's note names the value actually in effect. Supersedes the fallback part of D9b8061fd38.

[D6fc09b2590] The fallback is applied with source '<layer> (strictest fallback)', which config_wins treats as a config layer: the strictest value outranks a recorded flow choice (the file meant to set the knob, and D-enum-fallback-strict says a typo fails closed), 'flow show' reports the recorded choice as overridden, and adopt_defaults never records the fallback as the project's choice (pending excludes it).

[D-fallback-no-remote] Operator 2026-10-05 (AskUserQuestion on B-enum-strict-fallback): a bad config-file value for flow.integration falls back to 'merge' and for flow.claims to 'local', not 'pr' and 'remote'. General rule added to D-enum-fallback-strict: the fallback for a typo must never trigger an outward action (push, remote refs, forge API calls); outward behaviour happens only when someone sets it correctly on purpose. A test asserts that no KNOB_STRICTEST value enables remote or forge interaction. The warning and doctor still flag the typo.
data.title: Enum config knobs: declared choices, tolerated in files, fall back to the strictest value that never reaches the remote

data.decision:
[D-skills-spec-native] A ddflow-managed skill is a spec-compliant directory (SKILL.md + optional scripts/ references/ assets/) that any agent reads unchanged. ddflow-specific data (digest, source, version, sync state) lives in the event log and .ddflow/skills.lock, or in the spec's free-form metadata map, never in new frontmatter fields.

[D-skills-canonical-store] Default canonical store is .agents/skills/ (the cross-client convention); [skills].canonical can name another. 'ddflow skill sync' makes symlinks (default), copies, or generated files in each enabled agent's directory, marks what it manages, never overwrites a skill it did not create, and reports drift. Skills already in an agent directory are adopted, not moved, until the operator asks.

[D-skills-operator-answers] Decided by the operator 2026-10-03: (1) YAML parsing uses PyYAML with a colon-quote retry (add it as a dependency). (2) Skill sync defaults to COPY with drift detection against a managed sidecar; symlink is opt-in. (3) Install/pin use skills-lock.json at the repo root, compatible with the vercel format, with ddflow-namespaced fields (ref, commit, treeSha, hashAlgo, files) and a precisely defined full sha256 tree digest. (4) skill doctor: errors fail the exit code (1), warnings are advisory, and the report always says static checks only. (5) ddflow writes skills inside the repo only; user-level dirs ([REDACTED:path], [REDACTED:path]) are read-only for inventory unless [skills].user_level = true and an explicit command. (6) Agent-authored skills need a recorded human acknowledgement before they sync. (7) ddflow's invariants (brief first, claim before edit, the four enforced rules) stay in always-on context; skills carry only conditional procedures (onboard, review triage, verify, import, the driver), and an A/B adherence eval (B-skills-adherence-eval) precedes moving any instruction. (8) A Claude Code plugin named ddflow ships LAST, after the pack and sync are proven. DEFAULTS applied unless the operator objects (not asked): lint strictness is per-agent lenient (extras tolerated by agents are warnings 'rejected by skills-ref', not errors); names are ASCII on 'skill new' and NFKC-normalised on read; skills with scripts/, hooks, .mcp.json or bare Bash allowed-tools are installable only with a recorded approval; generated .mdc/Cline/AGENTS.md translations are committed with a do-not-edit banner; rules and skills stay separate record types with one shared 'what applies' view; MCP skill serving (SEP-2640) is opt-in later.
data.title: Skills: spec-native format, one canonical store synced into each agent, operator's answers

[D-no-duckdb] A description of the project claimed a SQLite and DuckDB index; a check found no DuckDB anywhere. The operator chose to correct the claim rather than build to it (2026-09-29).
data.decision:
[D-no-duckdb] Search and recall run on the derived SQLite index (.ddflow/index.db, FTS5 with BM25, LIKE fallback). ddflow does not add DuckDB. Semantic recall, if adopted (B-semantic-recall), stores its vectors in the same SQLite index.

[D-perf] Operator 2026-10-13 (AskUserQuestion, B-perf-decide), all defaults accepted. (1) NO DuckDB: D-no-duckdb stands, SQLite FTS5 is the only index (FTS5 measured 10-60x faster per query, 19 ms vs 222 ms startup, 13.5 MB vs 66 MB RSS); revisit an optional ddflow[analytics] extra only if the active log passes 500k events AFTER B-gap-log-scale. (2) NO REWRITE now; thresholds stored as [perf] budgets: hook p50 over 300 ms idle after the Python fixes -> a Rust/Go fast path for the hook subset only; fold+read over 3 s idle at the expected size after checkpoints, or resident MCP RSS over 1 GB, or an active log over 1M events -> a PyO3 core. (3) BUDGETS (idle machine, this repository's log; all configurable): ddflow --version 150 ms; hooks prompt 300 ms; hooks session-start 1.5 s; heartbeat 300 ms; status/next/brief 2 s; MCP initialize 1 s; fresh-process append 100 ms. (4) RESIDENT STATE: the MCP server caches the folded State by log digest; no new daemon (D-sched-no-daemon stands). (5) ORDER: the cheap fixes ride in B-gap-log-scale; the rest of P-perf follows it.
data.title: Performance and index: SQLite FTS5 only (no DuckDB), no rewrite now, budgets and resident state

data.alternatives:
[D-lean-and-trusted] consolidating tools (5% saving, breaks agents and parity tests); markdown for every read (breaks pinned JSON results); proposed-by-default imported decisions (operator declined); a remote server (a different product from the git-native design).

[D-mcp-output-schemas-off] On by default; on only for protocol 2025-06-18 and later clients.

[D-tools-list-budget-100k] Keeping the ratchet tight (raise by the measured cost of each tool, ~0.7 KB at a time): rejected by the operator as churn -- each new tool then needs its own reasoned raise and a re-measure. Raising it very high or removing it: not asked for, and it would remove the pressure that keeps descriptions trimmed.

[D-viewer-lists-consolidated] Adding `ddflow_bug_list` and `ddflow_lesson_list` as named tools (the item's literal request) -- rejected: they duplicate `ddflow_list kind=bug|lesson` and would need ~2 KB trimmed from existing tool descriptions to stay under the tools/list ratchet.
data.consequences:
[D-tools-list-budget-100k] A new MCP tool can land without a ratchet round for roughly the next three tools; the check still fails loudly once the list grows past 100,000, and shortening a description stays the first move. The cost: the list can grow by ~3 KB before anyone is forced to look at it, so the byte count is no longer a tight signal of tool-surface creep.

[D-viewer-lists-consolidated] Adding a listable kind means touching the engine and the consolidated tool's `kind`/filter properties, not adding a tool -- so tools/list stays bounded and every viewer shares one row shape, one redaction path and one `--json` contract. The cost: a kind that is NOT a viewer projection (needs its own data source) cannot be listed this way without extending the engine.

[D-lean-and-trusted] Research (2026-10-02, R-extres-evaluation) of an externally produced 'DDFlow MCP Extension Research' document against ddflow main. Verdict: a generic survey written from three Glama tool pages; ~2/3 of its proposals already exist in stronger form, ~1/4 conflict with ddflow's design (remote multi-tenant server, SSE/event bus, background LLM consolidation, tree-sitter/LSP/sqlite-vec/ONNX against the dependency allowlist, per-step full suite against the operator's batch-integration request); its load-bearing numbers (60-95% from tool consolidation, 70-85% from Markdown) rest on vendor/forum posts and could not be verified. Real gaps, MEASURED: (1) tools/list is 90 tools, 119 KB (~30k tokens) + 12 KB handshake text; the as_agent description repeats on 89 tools = 27 KB (22.7%); merging tools would save only ~5%; a 28-tool core set is 44 KB; (2) MCP read payloads are 28-35x their prose rendering: next 35 KB vs 1.2 KB CLI text, show 11 KB vs 1 KB, recall 32 KB, decision_list 40 KB, progress 150 KB; compact JSON alone saves only 10-37%; (3) no untrusted-data fencing or provenance: channels are PR-added event-log lines (merge=union, no signatures), imported ADRs becoming accepted decisions, agent-written records re-injected, PR review text, the reviewer diff in a single fence; (4) no model-tier hint on tasks; (5) no detector for the same gate failing the same way repeatedly; (6) ddflow_configure can set a non-human gate command to 'true' locally.

[D-mcp-output-schemas-off] On adds ~16 KB to tools/list (over the 95,000-byte budget) and sends every result twice.

[D-tools-list-budget-100k] The tools/list byte ratchet (tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py) had 9 bytes of headroom at 96,000, so adding ddflow_phase_close needed a documented raise to 96,800. Every new tool was going to need the same round.

[D-viewer-lists-consolidated] B196 predates `ddflow_list` (which consolidated the six viewers into one tool). Two named list tools would duplicate it, and the MCP tools/list byte budget is a hard ratchet with only ~700 bytes of headroom at the time. D-no-duplicates and D-lean-and-trusted push the same way.
data.decision:
[D-lean-and-trusted] Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-extres-evaluation): file and build all six: N1 B-mcp-schema-trim, N2 B-mcp-payload-bound, N3 B-mcp-tool-tiers, N4 B-security-provenance, N5 B-model-tier-hint, N6 B-repeated-failure-detector. (1) No tool is renamed or merged (agents' tool names and the CLI/MCP parity ratchets stay); the surface shrinks by trimming repeated descriptions and by an optional tier. (2) Payloads: bound/project the largest MCP reads; --json stays byte-identical to the CLI; brief/board stay markdown. (3) Provenance: imported ADRs and agent-recorded decisions KEEP status accepted (operator's choice, no change to onboarding); every decision/lesson/memory shown in brief, recall and import output carries who recorded it (decided_by / agent) and its source, and free-text bodies are fenced as data. (4) Defaults taken by the research recommendation (operator may revisit): the tool tier is a start-time knob [mcp].tools = core|standard|all (default all), no runtime expansion call in v1; the repeated-failure detector WARNS only (blocks only with an explicit on_detect = block); recording who changed a non-human gate command is added instead of making ddflow_configure operator-only. (5) Not built: remote multi-tenant server, SSE/event bus, tree-sitter/LSP, sqlite-vec/ONNX dependency, background LLM consolidation.

[D-mcp-output-schemas-off] Operator 2026-10-09: keep the knob off; typed outputSchema/structuredContent is opt-in.

[D-tools-list-budget-100k] TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET is raised to 100,000 (from 96,800) as an operator decision on 2026-10-12, to give the MCP tool list headroom instead of a reasoned raise per tool. Trimming a description remains the first move when a new tool pushes the list up; the budget is not a target to grow into.

[D-viewer-lists-consolidated] Bug, lesson, task, phase, research and session listing all go through the one MCP tool `ddflow_list` (selected by `kind`). A new record kind that should be listable is added to `services/viewers.KINDS` + `_FILTERS` + a row builder, surfaced on the CLI through `commands/viewers_lists.register`, and reached over MCP as `ddflow_list kind=<kind>` -- never as a tool of its own.

[D-quotas] Operator 2026-09-29 (session s20260929T105507-3319427): ddflow must support quotas generically, ask the agent (else the user) what they are, respect them, skip agents/LLMs with unlimited quotas; at 80% by default (unless the user asks to use everything) items in progress pause until the limit restarts and resume automatically (e.g. after 5h) unless the user says otherwise. data.decision:
[D-quotas] (1) A quota PROFILE per subject -- an agent harness+account (claude-code:<account>) or an LLM endpoint (llm:<base_url>): either unlimited, or windows {5h|day|week|month|total, limit, unit tokens|usd|sessions|vendor-percent, reset rolling|fixed}. (2) DISCOVERY: a subject with no profile is an obligation; the agent is asked first (MCP ddflow_quota declare) and answers from what it knows; if it cannot, it records 'unknown' and the operator is asked. Until declared, work is not blocked, only reminded. (3) METERS: prefer the vendor's own percent+reset (Claude Code statusline/stream-json/cache); otherwise count tokens/sessions locally; a reading that cannot be taken is UNAVAILABLE, never zero. (4) ENFORCEMENT at [quota] pause_at (default 0.8; 1.0 = use everything): next/claim refuse with exit 3 and resume_at (never exit 2, which the implement loop reads as done); items in progress PAUSE -- lease kept, expiry suspended, agent stops at a safe point (WIP committed); (5) RESUME automatically once the window resets and a fresh reading is below the threshold; operator 'quota hold' keeps it paused, 'quota continue' overrides now. (6) Profiles and usage samples are per USER account on this machine ([REDACTED:path], [REDACTED:path]), not the committed log; item pause/resume are project events. (7) ddflow does not call Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint with the user's credentials.

[D-governor] Operator 2026-10-12 accepted D-governor-proposal with these answers. (1) QUOTA MARKS 40/60/80: 40% caps new work at the balanced tier and medium effort; 60% caps at fast for mechanical work and low effort otherwise; 80% pause-and-ask (D-quotas). CONTEXT MARKS 60/75/85/95: 60% plan a checkpoint, 75% write the handoff, 85% compact or restart at the next safe point, 95% emergency checkpoint. All marks, tier caps and floors are [govern] knobs (D-everything-configurable). (2) STOP-AND-ASK for a headless pipeline = PAUSE AND WAIT AND NOTIFY: items pause with the lease kept (D-quotas), the pipeline takes no new work and records the question; it waits for 'quota continue' (CLI, MCP or a prompt answer) and otherwise resumes by itself at the window reset. (3) Defaults for the questions not asked, all configurable: tier names stay fast|balanced|deep and map to models per harness in the model registry (declared, never hard-coded); the operator may override anything at any time; an agent may override only what [govern] allows. Everything else in D-governor-proposal stands.

The old records are superseded by this one and keep their text in the log. Every section below is the recorded text of the source named in brackets, unchanged. The four sources were each decided by the operator, but this record is a synthesis written by the agent of the operator's D-roadmap-review item 2, so it is attributed to the agent.

[D-upgrade-auto-check] Proposed D-upgrade-model; research R-upgrade-experiment.

[D-self-upgrade] Phase B-upgrade; research R-upgrade-experiment (no version stamp, no changelog, stale MCP servers undetected, hooks pin a binary path).

data.decision:
CURRENT RULE (the operator's D-roadmap-review item 2, 2026-10-14, quoted as recorded): (2) UPGRADE: session start only prints the one-line notice ([upgrade].auto=check); on MCP connect the agent proposes the upgrade and the operator consents; container start applies safe categories only, and only when [upgrade].auto is safe.

The four superseded records follow as recorded. Where one of them says otherwise on writes (D-self-upgrade (5) and D-self-upgrade-defaults let container or MCP start apply safe categories under [upgrade].on_start = safe; D-upgrade-auto-check makes safe an opt-in), the rule above governs. Release check, self-upgrade command, consent and rollback, and orchestrate-and-monitor from D-self-upgrade stand as recorded. Other upgrade records (D-upgrade-event-kinds, D-upgrade-backups, D-upgrade-config-changes, D-upgrade-manifest-lint, D-upgrade-skew-guard, D-dry-run-from-running-version, D-start-timeout-note) are not replaced.

[D-upgrade-auto-check] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Should [upgrade].auto ship as check - go for check'. [upgrade].auto = off|check|safe, shipped default check for every ddflow project: after ddflow is upgraded, the first session start on a machine prints one line (once per machine per version) such as 'ddflow upgraded 0.1.9 -> 0.1.10: run ddflow upgrade --plan' and writes nothing. safe (agents apply non-destructive categories) and off are configurable via config, CLI and MCP. Still OPEN in D-upgrade-model: skew guard default (operator proposed refuse-once with a recorded override flag), backup location, operator-only default changes, manifest lint. Accepted so far: D-upgrade-event-kinds.

[D-self-upgrade] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Make ddflow have a feature to periodically check for newer versions of ddflow, to propose to the operator upgrade of itself, to have self-upgrade cli command and capabilities which do migration and upgrades (in case of running docker it shall introduce check for upgrade and migration on container or mcp start and implement it while in container if the container version has been upgraded and database and other storage and config artifacts needs migration) need. The user should be capable to check, ask, request ddflow upgrade and orchestrate and monitor it'. Recorded design (defaults chosen by claude where the operator did not say; each is a knob the operator can change): (1) RELEASE CHECK: ddflow looks for a newer release of itself at most once per [upgrade].check_interval_h (default 24) from the package index it was installed from (and the image registry tag when running in a container); opportunistic at session start/brief/doctor, never a daemon, bounded by a short timeout, silent and harmless offline; the result is cached under .ddflow/local; it sends nothing but the request for the public version list (no project data, no telemetry). [upgrade].release_check = on|off (shipped default on, because the operator asked for periodic checks; off for air-gapped use; DDFLOW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK env). (2) PROPOSAL: a newer release is PROPOSED, never installed silently: one line in the session-start notice, brief, status and doctor ('ddflow X is available, you run Y: what changed + how to upgrade'), once per version per machine; an agent that sees it tells the operator. (3) SELF-UPGRADE: `ddflow upgrade --self` (CLI; MCP ddflow_upgrade action=self) detects how ddflow is installed (uv tool, pipx, pip in a venv, uvx/ephemeral, container image, source checkout) and either runs the right installer command or, where it cannot (container image, source checkout, read-only install), prints the exact command for the operator; installing new code is the operator's decision: an agent may run it only with the operator's recorded consent ([upgrade].self = ask|operator|auto, default ask); the old version is remembered so `ddflow upgrade --self --rollback` can reinstall it. (4) MIGRATION follows the install: after a self-upgrade, and on the first run of a new version, the project upgrade plan runs (ddflow upgrade --plan), and the categories allowed by [upgrade].auto are applied with a backup first; operator-set config needs confirmation (D-upgrade-config-changes). (5) CONTAINER / MCP START: when the server or the container starts, it compares its own version with the project's stamp (and the stores it mounts: log, index, local config, backups, hooks, instruction files); if the image is newer it runs the check and the safe migrations in the container before serving, reports what it did or what awaits the operator in the first brief, and never fails to start because of a pending migration (it serves, marks the plan pending and says so); if the image is OLDER than the project the skew guard applies (D-upgrade-skew-guard). [upgrade].on_start = check|safe|off (default safe for index/derived-store rebuilds and non-destructive categories; anything needing consent waits). (6) ORCHESTRATE AND MONITOR: the operator can ask at any time: ddflow upgrade --check (is there a newer release, is this project behind), --plan, --apply, --self, --status (what ran, what is pending, which agents/MCP servers still run the old version and must restart), --history, --restore; the same over MCP so the operator can ask an agent; every step is recorded as events so replay explains it; a running upgrade shows progress and can be resumed after an interruption (idempotent steps).

[D-self-upgrade-defaults] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'I agree with your defaults'. Confirms the three defaults claude chose in D-self-upgrade: [upgrade].release_check = on (an outbound request for the public version list only, no project data; off or DDFLOW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK disables it; README states what is requested); [upgrade].self = ask (an agent installs new code only with the operator's recorded consent); [upgrade].on_start = safe (container/MCP start applies derived-store rebuilds and non-destructive backed-up categories; consent items wait). All remain configurable via config, CLI and MCP.

[D-upgrade-on-mcp-connect] Operator 2026-10-09: when the operator restarts and connects to the new MCP version it must detect the version difference by itself and start the upgrade, asking the operator for permission; nothing is applied without that consent.
data.title: Upgrade flow: session start prints a notice only; on MCP connect the agent proposes and the operator consents; container start applies safe categories only

The recent window is one hour with at least 10 outcomes, so one failure is 10% of it: against a clean or near-clean week that alone is 2x-200x, and the limit would shrink for the whole hour on noise. Reviewers (deepseek, kilo) objected both to ignoring clean baselines (None), to a fixed 1/20 floor (hides a reliable project's tenfold jump) and to the lone-failure cap (masks a single-failure 2x).

Accepted as it stands by the operator (D-roadmap-review item 4, 2026-10-14; recorded by RH-merge-decisions), superseding the proposed record D-gate-ratio-noise.
data.decision: ratio = recent rate / (max(baseline failures, 1) / baseline outcomes); None under 10 recent or 20 baseline outcomes; when the recent hour has fewer than 2 failures the ratio is capped at 1.0. No critical mark ships for the ratio, so only 'over 2.0' matters (magnitude never pauses admission).

chunk_findings.detail: The doc's own header claims its authority is the operator's item 8, which permits superseding records only for *pure merges* ("pure merges may be made as superseding records without asking per group"). The D-skills row is not a pure merge: as the "Left for the operator" section concedes, D-skills-canonical-store says `sync` makes symlinks by default while D-skills-operator-answers says `sync` defaults to copy, and the agent-authored D-skills record deliberately leaves both quoted without deciding which governs. Nevertheless the table already applies the supersede verb to all three sources, so after this change `ddflow decision show D-skills-operator-answers` returns a superseded record and no current record determines the default: any reader/consumer that resolves the current text for `ddflow sync` (copy vs symlink) now has two conflicting quoted sections and no authoritative answer, whereas before the change the operator-attributed D-skills-operator-answers governed. That inverts the precedence stated in D-rules-hierarchy (project/operator rules outrank agent defaults — D-skills is marked "Decided by: agent"): an agent-trust record has displaced the operator's rule on a point the agent record does not actually settle, so the supersession here is both unauthorized by the cited item 8 ("pure merge") and unresolved. The D-upgrade-flow row has the same shape (the agent record "states item 2 as the current rule" over D-self-upgrade-defaults' `[upgrade].on_start = safe`, a content change, not a pure merge), so the fix should either hold back the supersede until the operator rules per group, or mark the new records as proposed rather than current.

chunk_findings.detail:
The document's stated authority is the operator's item 8, which permits *"pure merges ... as superseding records without asking per group."* A pure merge is one that combines decisions that agree. The D-skills row, however, supersedes a record that disagrees with the others: the bullet at line 21 says *"D-skills-canonical-store says sync makes symlinks by default; D-skills-operator-answers says sync defaults to copy. Both are quoted; which governs is the operator's call."* The row's own attribution ("agent (two sources carry no operator attribution)") makes clear that the remaining source, D-skills-operator-answers, *does* carry operator attribution — it is the operator's answer that the merge contradicts. So an agent-authored record (`D-skills`, "Decided by: agent") supersedes an operator-attributed decision on a point the document itself concedes is unresolved and is "the operator's call." Concrete result: after this change `ddflow decision show D-skills-operator-answers` returns a superseded record and the sync default is no longer "copy" — the operator's answer has been overridden with agent text before the operator was asked, which is outside the "pure merges" delegation the file cites as its authority. The same row also violates the intent statement "nothing is reworded beyond the operator's answers": here an agent-written record is the current carrier of a point the operator had already answered.

(Note: I checked the other groups against the intent's counts — export 4, enum fallback 4, skills 3, MCP surface 4, ordering 7, perf 2, quotas+governor 2 — and they match, so I am reporting only the D-skills authority/attribution issue.)
